review.brief: Review RM24-gateway-add-i18n-foundation (tier 2 of RM24-i18n-translations), module `gateway`, commits 01ca611 (wave 1: i18n package, middleware, LangSwitch) and 331fd05 (wave 2: ui.LangSwitcher, translated nav shell, docs). Review the DIFF, not the module. Validate: (1) SECURITY PREMISE — setLangCookie MUST call c.SetSameSite(http.SameSiteLaxMode) BEFORE c.SetCookie, and TestLangSwitch_CookieIsSameSiteLax must exist unweakened. The user approved omitting CSRF on POST /ui/lang/switch ONLY on that condition (design.md D8); its absence or weakening is a BLOCKER. (2) Module boundaries — no HTML outside gateway; language reached ONLY via account.Service on Deps, never internal/account/db; internal/gateway/i18n imports nothing beyond context + account. (3) UI stack rules — no DaisyUI component class inlined in pages/fragments/layouts NEWLY by this change (note: base.templ's `btn btn-square btn-ghost` pre-exists on main and is out of scope); semantic theme tokens only, no hex; NO client-side JS added; no HTML comments in .templ. (4) Behaviour vs spec — signed-in reads accounts.language, anonymous reads the lang cookie, both fall back to es; an unrecognized value resolves to es and never breaks a render; the cookie syncs with the DB value; HX-Location carries path+query so the switch does not disrupt the page. (5) Catalogue completeness is enforced by TestCatalog_AllKeysHaveBothLanguages, and AGENTS.md now carries a BINDING EN+ES rule for new labels (MAG-8 asked for this explicitly — check the wording is binding, not advisory). (6) Codegen — *_templ.go regenerated and static/app.css committed (the module CI guard). (7) Performance — language resolved ONCE per request in middleware, carried on context; the switcher adds no per-render DB read. (8) Anti-gaming — no task title or criterion weakened; every ticked checkbox genuinely done; wave 1's guard test not touched by wave 2. Escalate on doubt: return changes-requested rather than approving anything uncertain.

findings.note: tasks.md T6.4 (checked [x], progress.json T6.4 marked done) requires adding `internal/gateway/templates/fragments/nav_header_test.go` (new, if none exists) with `TestNavHeader_StatusLabelTranslatesPerLanguage` — rendering `NavHeaderVM{Status: NavStatusConnected}` under both `i18n.WithLang(ctx, LanguageES)` and `...LanguageEN`, asserting the two renders differ and each matches the catalogue's `KeyNavHeaderStatusConnected` entry. No such file or test exists anywhere in the repo (`grep -rn 'StatusLabelTranslatesPerLanguage\|statusLabelKeyFor\|Conectado\|Dormido' internal/gateway --include='*_test.go'` returns nothing). The only fragment-level nav-header test, `TestNavHeaderFragment_ConnectedHTTP` in handlers_test.go, asserts on `badge-success`/`94%`/vehicle name but never on the rendered status word text in either language, and its engine (`navHeaderEngine`) never registers `LanguageMiddleware`, so it exercises no language variation at all. T6.4's handlers_test.go half (removing the four `vm.StatusLabel` assertions) was done correctly, but the fragments-test half of the same task was not — the checkbox and progress.json note both claim it complete ('handlers_test.go: removed StatusLabel assertions...') without disclosing the missing fragments test. This is the exact kind of partially-done-but-ticked task item 8 of the brief asks the reviewer to catch. The underlying code (`statusLabelKeyFor` + `i18n.T(ctx, ...)` in nav_header.templ) reads correctly on inspection, so this is a test-coverage/anti-gaming gap, not a known behavioral defect — hence major, not blocker.

Re-verified against fix commit 2ea08d9: internal/gateway/templates/fragments/nav_header_test.go adds TestNavHeader_StatusLabelTranslatesPerLanguage (table-driven over all 4 NavHeaderStatusKind values) and TestNavHeader_ConnectPromptTranslates. Ran both directly — all subtests pass. Confirmed the test is not a tautology: for each status it asserts the ES render contains the catalogue's ES string AND the EN render contains the catalogue's EN string (not just an es==en inequality check) — a regression that hardcoded English, or dropped the i18n.T(ctx, statusLabelKeyFor(...)) call in favor of a literal, would fail the ES-side strings.Contains, since every one of the 4 status catalogue entries has genuinely distinct ES/EN text (verified against catalog.go: Conectado/Connected, Dormido/Asleep, Esperando primer dato/Awaiting first snapshot, No disponible/Unavailable). The redundant es==en check adds a second, independent tripwire for the same regression class. Traced renderNavHeader's use of templ.Handler(NavHeader(vm)).Component.Render(ctx, &buf) — same ctx-threading pattern already proven correct by this change's other passing context-based tests (TestBase_RendersLangSwitcher, lang_switcher_test.go), so no reason to doubt it exercises the real ctx path.

decisions.decision: Approved omitting a CSRF token on POST /ui/lang/switch, CONDITIONAL on the lang cookie being SameSite=Lax
decisions.why: The module has a close CSRF precedent (vehicle-select, handlers.go:529) but it is auth-only and cannot transplant to a control that must work for anonymous login-page visitors without minting a session for every one of them. SameSite=Lax blocks the cross-site POST; worst-case abuse is a one-click-reversible language flip.

decisions.decision: Amended design.md D8 and tasks T2.1/T3.5 to make SameSite=Lax explicit and test-enforced
decisions.why: The worker's design never mentioned SameSite, and T2.1 specified gin's c.SetCookie(...) which has NO SameSite parameter — as written it would have produced a cookie without the attribute, silently voiding the premise the user approved. Added the mandatory c.SetSameSite call, the full normative cookie-attribute spec, and a non-droppable TestLangSwitch_CookieIsSameSiteLax.

decisions.decision: Split tier 2 implementation into 2 serial waves (T1-T3 Go layer, then T4-T8 templates/docs/verify) instead of one 35-task dispatch
decisions.why: The artifact dispatch alone consumed 260k subagent tokens; one 35-task implementation worker risks exhausting context mid-change and returning partial work. The split also sequences handlers.go (T3.4 and T6.3 both edit it) instead of risking a concurrent conflict.

decisions.decision: Accepted reviewer finding R1 and fixed it directly rather than re-dispatching the worker
decisions.why: Independently confirmed: T6.4 names TestNavHeader_StatusLabelTranslatesPerLanguage, it existed nowhere in the repo, and the checkbox was ticked — a genuine anti-gaming catch. The fix is one focused test file inside the module; a full worker re-dispatch would re-read the whole doc pack for it.
